finding.sequence_description: Direct JWT endpoint: attempt alg=none unsigned JWT acceptance vs a valid signed control JWT under the same role.
finding.description:

sequence.description: Direct JWT endpoint: attempt alg=none unsigned JWT acceptance vs a valid signed control JWT under the same role.

finding.sequence_description: Direct JWT endpoint: demonstrate control acceptance with trusted key, then rotate trust anchor and attempt login with a JWT signed by the previously-trusted key (should be rejected).
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_oldkey_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_oldkey_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted a JWT signed by a key that should no longer be trusted after rotation; verification policy may not match consumed proof.

sequence.description: Direct JWT endpoint: demonstrate control acceptance with trusted key, then rotate trust anchor and attempt login with a JWT signed by the previously-trusted key (should be rejected).
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I1: After trust-anchor rotation, Vault must verify signatures against the current configured key set only. Accepting a JWT signed by an old/untrusted key indicates verification policy mismatch vs consumed proof.

finding.sequence_description: I1 kid-injection/key-confusion probe: configure static trusted pubkeys, then attempt login with a JWT that advertises a malicious kid and is signed by an untrusted key. Secure behavior: reject. If accepted, verification may be using attacker-selected key material rather than configured trust.
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_kid_injection_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_kid_injection_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted an attacker-signed JWT by honoring attacker-controlled kid/key selection rather than configured jwt_validation_pubkeys.

sequence.description: I1 kid-injection/key-confusion probe: configure static trusted pubkeys, then attempt login with a JWT that advertises a malicious kid and is signed by an untrusted key. Secure behavior: reject. If accepted, verification may be using attacker-selected key material rather than configured trust.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I1: Vault must verify JWT signatures only against configured trust keys, not against attacker-controlled key selection via kid/header tricks. Accepting an attacker-signed token indicates proof verification is not applied to the consumed proof.

params.description: jwt mount for I1 kid injection

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login failed; static key trust may be misconfigured, invalidating the kid-injection probe.

finding.sequence_description: JWT trust anchor rotation: accept key-A baseline, rotate to key-B, then ensure key-A-signed JWT is rejected on new login (no stale JWKS/pubkey cache).
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attack_old_keyA_after_rotation_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attack_old_keyA_after_rotation_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Login with old key-A succeeded after trust rotated to key-B (stale trust anchor / non-atomic validation).

sequence.description: JWT trust anchor rotation: accept key-A baseline, rotate to key-B, then ensure key-A-signed JWT is rejected on new login (no stale JWKS/pubkey cache).
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I3: After admin rotates the configured JWT validation public keys, new logins must be validated against the updated trust anchor immediately; previously trusted signatures must not remain accepted.

params.description: jwt mount for I3 signing-key rotation test

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline key-A login failed; cannot evaluate key rotation coherence.

finding.sequence_description: I4 identity-claim switch: change role identity_claim from sub to email and re-authenticate two distinct principals that share email to detect unintended identity collapse after config mutation.

sequence.description: I4 identity-claim switch: change role identity_claim from sub to email and re-authenticate two distinct principals that share email to detect unintended identity collapse after config mutation.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I4: After an admin changes identity_claim, two distinct upstream principals (different sub) that share a common email may collapse into the same downstream entity (principal boundary loss due to claim selection change).
